data.summary: The `rust` directory is a single scenario package in an `aio-config` generator system: it declares how to install the Rust toolchain (via mise's `core:rust` backend, which internally drives rustup) on top of a base image. `scenario.toml` holds the declarative metadata (id, category, installer, selectable versions) consumed by `aio-config gen`, while `fragment.Dockerfile` holds the actual executable install steps that the generator stitches into a final Dockerfile. The two files work as a metadata + implementation pair and carry unusually detailed inline rationale about why the config-table form and a non-minimal rustup profile are required.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs the Rust toolchain through mise's `core:rust`/rustup backend, appending a table-form rust config and running `mise install rust`. It documents two mandatory compensations: forcing `profile = "default"` and installing to a system path to avoid rustup's minimal profile and volume-shadowing issues.
file_insights.source_summary: A Dockerfile fragment consisting of a heavily commented header followed by shell/RUN steps: append `rust = { version = "...", profile = "default" }` to the mise config using `>>`, then execute `mise install rust` against the core:rust backend (rustup under the hood) to materialize the toolchain at /opt/mise. The comments document the version/profile requirement, the ~1.4GB install size, and the two non-negotiable compensations for a fresh RUSTUP_HOME.
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment is the L3 'lang' layer of the image build: it installs the full Rust toolchain (rustc, cargo, clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer) into /opt/mise so system paths survive volume shadowing. Because `mise use -g` can only emit the simple `rust = "1.93.1"` form rather than the required table form with `profile`, the fragment appends the config block directly with `>>` (composable with other fragments) and then explicitly runs `mise install rust`. The header comments record PoC-verified reasoning dated 2026-09-02 explaining why each compensation is necessary.
responsibilities: Install the complete Rust toolchain via mise core:rust/rustup
Append a table-form rust entry (version + profile) to the mise config instead of using `mise use -g`
Force the rustup `default` profile so clippy/rustfmt/rust-analyzer are present
Install to the system path /opt/mise to avoid persistence-volume shadowing
Remain composable with other fragments by appending rather than overwriting config

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Declarative scenario metadata for the Rust installation, consumed by `aio-config gen` for fragment resolution: it defines the id, display name/description, category `lang`, installer `mise`, and the selectable version list (e.g. 1.93.1) injected into the fragment as `{{version}}`.
file_insights.source_summary: A TOML document with fields `id = "rust"`, `name = "Rust"`, `description` (mise core:rust backend, clippy/rustfmt/rust-analyzer components, installed to /opt/mise, ~1.4GB, largest mise tool), `category = "lang"`, `installer = "mise"`, plus a `[[versions]]` array holding label entries such as `1.93.1`. Comments explain that `gen` injects `{{version}}` and that the fragment must use the table form rather than `mise use -g`.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the discovery/registry side of the scenario: the generator reads it to know that a `rust` scenario exists, what category and installer it belongs to, and which versions the TUI should offer in its dropdown. Its inline comments explicitly warn that rust's fragment cannot use plain `mise use -g` and must write the table form with a profile, cross-referencing fragment.Dockerfile. Together with the fragment it forms the complete, self-contained definition of one installable language toolchain.
responsibilities: Register the `rust` scenario for `aio-config gen` fragment resolution
Declare category (`lang`) and installer backend (`mise`) for TUI grouping/filtering
Provide the selectable version list that drives the TUI dropdown
Supply a human-readable name and size/composition description
Document the version-injection contract (`{{version}}`) for the adjacent fragment
